The corpus

Every molecule in OpenScent v1.0candidate

A CC0 structure–odour corpus built only from US patents and US-government databases. Each odour tag below is a word quoted verbatim from its source, with the sentence one click away. Nothing is generated.

MoleculeOdour tagsFormulaMWXLogP3QuotesStructure
No molecule matches these filters.
Formula, MW and XLogP3 are values computed by PubChem (NCBI) and read from its record for the molecule; a dash means PubChem has no record for this exact structure, or no value. Click a column head to sort.
Lightest to heaviest. Here the dots are placed by molecular weight, in rows by family. Drag the blend slider to melt them back into the scent map, drag the two weight handles to keep a band, or press Sweep.
Scent mapWeight ladder
Each dot is a molecule, placed by how its sources describe it (the pattern of odour tags; t-SNE). Molecules with the same pattern form a tight group; position inside a group means nothing. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, click a dot to read its quotes. Colours are a display aid, not a classification. Close on the map means described alike, not smelling alike.
The 67 odour terms, not the molecules. Dot area = molecules carrying the term; a dark ring = the term reaches the 30-molecule bar; lines join terms that often appear on the same molecules (same method as the scent map, so distances are approximate). Click a term to list its molecules.
The same terms by number of molecules. The amber mark is the 30-molecule bar.

CC0 1.0 for the data; code Apache-2.0. A molecule appearing here says nothing about live patent claims covering it. Odour words describe what the sources say about smell; they are not claims about health or effects. Rows set aside by the model screen were not read by a human, so absence here is a recall limit, not a judgement.
